newsitem.title: LATVIA: DIVIDENDS TO BE PAID VIA DEPOSITORY.
newsitem.headline: DIVIDENDS TO BE PAID VIA DEPOSITORY.

text.p: Latvia's central depository said on Thursday it has introduced new rules for the payment of dividends, which means payments will be made via the depository.
"Dividend payments will take place through the depository, which is the accepted practice elsewhere in the world," depository president Martinsh Rikshis told a news conference.
The regulations, effective from March 14, provide for dividends or interest on fixed interest paper to be paid through both the depository and account holders, brokerages or banks.
A company will transfer money on the pay day into the depository account, which transfers it to the account holder.
The account holder will transfer money into the account of the share owner, he added.
The depository has to receive information on the dividend calculation date, the payment date and the amount to be paid.
The calculation date has to be set at an earliest 10 days after a decision on dividend payment has been taken.
The payment day has to be set earliest on the third day after the calculation date.
This would replace the earlier practice whereby the company informed about the amount of money it has to transfer to the account holder without the actual transfer of money through the depository.
